title: Career Lattice and Skill-Badging Program — Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines Redwood's Career Lattice and the accompanying Skill-Badging Program. It standardizes role-level expectations, clarifies promotion and rotation processes, and ties skill badges to onboarding, performance calibration, and benefits pathways.

Audience: People managers, individual contributors, people-ops partners, hiring managers, and engineers preparing for role changes or promotions.

Goals

- Make career progression transparent across functions (Engineering, Product, Research, Sales, and GTM).
- Enable horizontal movement (rotations and lateral moves) without penalty to total comp trajectory.
- Provide portable, verifiable skill badges that reflect applied competency rather than tenure.
- Reduce time-to-contribution for internal transferees and new hires by aligning onboarding bundles to lattice tracks.

Scope and Definitions

- "Career Lattice": a multidimensional framework connecting Level (IC/Manager), Functional Specializations (e.g., Serving Runtime, Observability), and Cross-Functional Skills (e.g., System Design, Security).
- "Skill Badge": a lightweight credential issued by People Ops + engineering reviewers to attest to demonstrated competence (evidence-based). Badges are recorded in the internal HR profile and visible to hiring managers.
- This playbook covers: level definitions (L1–L7), promotion cadence, lateral/rotation process, badging criteria, onboarding tie-ins, and tooling integrations.

Level Structure (high level)

- L1 (Associate): Early-career contributors; focus on onboarding, mentorship, and core execution.
- L2 (Engineer / Associate PM): Executes independently on well-scoped work; owns small components.
- L3 (Senior / Staff individual contributor path entry): Leads medium-complexity projects; mentors peers.
- L4 (Senior Staff / Manager): Leads cross-team initiatives or manages teams; defines technical strategy for a domain.
- L5 (Principal / Group Manager): Shapes product/technical direction across multiple teams.
- L6+ (Distinguished / Director+): Company-level impact and strategy.

Sample competency table (use for calibration meetings)

| Dimension | L2 | L3 | L4 | L5 |
|-----------|----|----|----|----|
| Ownership | Owns tasks end-to-end with guidance | Owns components independently | Owns cross-team features and tradeoffs | Shapes org-level priorities |
| Design | Implements straightforward designs | Designs systems for scalability | Architects multi-service flows | Defines technical principles |
| Communication | Clear within team | Influences cross-team discussions | Shapes product requirements with stakeholders | Influences executive audience |

Promotion Process (concise procedure)

1. Candidate raises interest to manager and updates Career Profile (People Ops portal).
2. Manager completes Promotion Nomination form (template) with: scope of work, artifacts (PRs, design docs), 3+ peer reviewer names, impact metrics, and expected level.
3. Peer reviewers provide written feedback via the People Ops review form within 10 business days.
4. Calibration panel (people-ops + cross-functional senior reviewers) meets in monthly promotion windows. Promotion decisions documented in HR system.
5. If approved, onboarding checklist is generated for new level-specific expectations and skill-badge opportunities. Timeline target: decision within 30 days of nomination.

Criteria and Evidence (examples)

- Evidence-based artifacts: merged PRs, production metrics, incident leadership notes, design docs, customer impact summaries, and mentoring examples.
- Minimum impact expectation: at least one measurable cross-team outcome (reliability, latency, cost, adoption) for moves to L4+.
- Time-in-role is advisory, not prescriptive: rapid promotions permitted with strong evidence.

Lateral Moves and Rotations

Principles

- Rotations are encouraged and treated as formal development assignments (3–6 months typical).
- Compensation and continuous benefits remain intact during rotations; compensation reviews align to the receiving role post-rotation based on outcomes.

Process (for internal applicants)

1. Candidate and receiving manager agree on objectives and success metrics; submit Rotation Agreement to People Ops.
2. People Ops validates capacity and confirms reporting/mentorship structures.
3. Rotation kickoff includes a 2-week focused onboarding bundle (see Onboarding tie-ins below).

Skill-Badging Program

Overview: Skill badges are small, earned credentials tied to discrete competencies (e.g., "Production Deployment Ownership", "Large-Scale Embeddings Ops", "Cross-Region Networking for Private Deployments"). Badges are earned through a combination of: documented artifacts, peer review, and a short applied assessment where relevant.

Badge lifecycle

- Nomination: Candidate submits evidence and supporting reviewers.
- Panel review: A triage panel (one senior engineer from the domain, one people-ops reviewer, one cross-functional verifier) evaluates evidence within 7 business days.
- Issuance: Badge appears on internal profile and can be linked in promotion packages. Badges may expire after 24 months for areas with fast-moving tech; renewal requires re-evidence.

Badging examples and acceptance criteria (examples)

- "Service Observability Badge": evidence = design doc + 2 production alerts resolved + postmortem contribution.
- "Deploy Pipeline Steward": evidence = authored CI/CD config, 1 rollout owned, runbook updates.

Onboarding Tie-ins (how new hires use the lattice)

- New hires complete a Role Profile survey during week 1 that maps their prior badges and preferred tracks.
- People Ops assigns an onboarding bundle: required reading, mentor pairing, and an initial small project aligned to the lattice track.
- Within 60 days, hiring manager and new hire propose 90-day success metrics tied to potential badges.

Benefits and Performance Alignment

- Compensation: Promotions follow the published compensation bands per level; skill badges inform merit and bonus calibrations but do not replace formal compensation processes.
- Learning stipends: Badge earners are eligible for an accelerated learning stipend (up to $1,200/year) for role-relevant training.

Tools and Workflow Integrations

- People Ops portal: central repository for profiles, nominations, and badges. (Integration: HRIS must support custom badge fields.)
- GitHub/GitLab: artifact linking required for most badges (PRs, commit hashes).
- Internal Wiki/Confluence: canonical place for design docs and evidence.
- Slack: dedicated #career-lattice channel for badge Q&A and rotation openings.

Governance and Ownership

- Program owner: People Ops (Aisha Patel).
- Technical badge stewards: Rotating roster of senior engineers (2 per domain) who serve 6-month terms.
- Review cadence: Quarterly program health review (metrics below) and annual policy refresh.

Metrics and Success Measures

- Time-to-promotion (median). Target: <= 10 months for level-to-level where applicable.
- Percentage of promotions with at least one skill badge on file. Target: 60%+ by end of first year.
- Rotation success rate (rotation converted to permanent placement or marked successful). Target: 70%.

Communications and Rollout Plan

- Phase 1 (Q4 2024): Pilot with Eng platform and People Ops; publish initial 8 badges.
- Phase 2 (Q1 2025): Expand to Product and Research; automation for badge issuance.
- Full rollout (Q2 2025): Company-wide announcement, manager training sessions, and incorporation into performance calibration.

Appendix A: Promotion checklist (manager-facing)

- Updated Career Profile (candidate)
- Promotion Nomination form completed
- 3+ reviewer statements collected
- Artifact links included (PRs, metrics, postmortems)
- Calibration panel submission deadline met

Appendix B: Example Rotation Agreement fields

- Candidate name, current role, receiving manager, rotation length, objectives (3 items), success metrics, mentor assigned, expected end-date.

Questions and escalation

- First point of contact: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai).
- For disputes: escalate to Head of People Ops and a designated cross-functional appeals panel.

Revision history

- 2024-11-03: Playbook created (pilot scope).
- 2025-02-14: Clarified badge lifecycle and added compensation tie-ins.
